title: DesignBid
problem_statement: Product and engineering teams at seed and Series A startups need high-quality product design for 2-8 week sprints but lack the runway to hire a full-time designer at $130-160K/year. Existing freelance platforms like Upwork surface 200+ unvetted candidates per post and require 10-15 hours of portfolio review and test assignment coordination before a team can start work. Agencies charge $15-25K retainers that are out of reach for pre-Series B companies. The result is that product teams either hire too slowly and ship without design, or default to a generalist agency and receive work that doesn't fit their product aesthetic. A curated marketplace of pre-vetted product designers with standardized portfolio reviews, transparent sprint-based pricing, and async trial projects can cut hiring time from 3 weeks to 3 days for early-stage product teams.
target_users: Product managers and founders at seed-to-Series A startups (5-50 employees) hiring product designers for 2-8 week sprints
CTOs and engineering leads at early-stage companies who make design hiring decisions without a dedicated talent function
Freelance product designers with 3+ years of experience who want consistent project flow without self-marketing on Upwork
Design team leads at mid-size companies backfilling design capacity during peak product cycles without adding headcount
user_stories: As a product manager at a startup, I want to browse a curated list of pre-vetted product designers filtered by specialty (mobile, web, design systems) and availability so that I can shortlist 3 candidates in under an hour without reading 200 Upwork profiles
As a startup founder, I want to see a designer's case studies formatted to show problem, process, and outcome — not just final screens — so that I can assess their thinking before scheduling a call

As a hiring product manager, I want to post a brief 4-hour paid trial task and receive completed work from up to 3 candidates before committing to a sprint engagement so that I can evaluate actual work quality rather than relying on portfolio alone

As a freelance product designer, I want to set my available sprint slots and rate per week and be matched with inbound client briefs rather than bidding on open posts so that I spend time designing instead of writing proposals
As a startup founder, I want transparent sprint-based pricing (weekly rate x sprint length) with no hidden agency fees so that I can budget a design engagement without negotiating over scope
As a hiring product manager, I want to extend a sprint engagement by 1 or 2 weeks mid-sprint with a single click so that I don't lose momentum when the project scope grows

As a freelance designer, I want payment released automatically 48 hours after each weekly deliverable is approved or the approval window expires so that I am not chasing invoices at the end of a sprint
acceptance_criteria: Designer applicants complete a structured vetting process: portfolio submission, a 2-hour paid design exercise, and a 30-minute video screen; fewer than 20% of applicants receive marketplace access, with acceptance criteria documented and applied consistently by a DesignBid reviewer
The marketplace displays only designers with confirmed availability in the client's requested sprint window; availability is updated by designers weekly and flagged as stale if not updated in 7 days

Clients can post a trial task brief, receive completed submissions from up to 3 matched designers, and select one to start a sprint — all within 5 business days of posting; SLA is displayed to clients at brief submission

Sprint pricing is shown as a flat weekly rate; the total engagement cost (rate x weeks) is displayed before the client confirms a booking, with no additional charges except a 12% platform fee disclosed at checkout

Sprint extension (1 or 2 additional weeks at the same weekly rate) can be confirmed by the client with a single button click before the final day of the current sprint; designer must accept or decline within 24 hours

Designer payment is released automatically 48 hours after the client approves a weekly deliverable or the 48-hour approval window expires without client action; payment appears in the designer's Stripe balance within 2 business days of release
A new client can complete signup, post a brief, and receive their first designer shortlist within 30 minutes of account creation, excluding vetting pipeline time for the designers themselves

All designer-client communication occurs through the DesignBid messaging thread; off-platform contact details may not be exchanged until after the first completed sprint, enforced by moderation policy

success_metrics.metric: Median time from brief submission to sprint start (business days)
success_metrics.baseline: Client interviews report 3-week average to hire a freelance designer via Upwork including trial tasks
success_metrics.target: Median brief-to-sprint-start under 5 business days within 3 months of launch

success_metrics.metric: Sprint completion rate (sprints that reach the agreed end date without early termination by either party)
success_metrics.baseline: No baseline; early termination signals poor matching quality; freelance platform norms suggest 85-90% completion for curated marketplaces
success_metrics.target: Sprint completion rate above 88% within 6 months of launch

success_metrics.metric: Sprint repeat rate (clients who book a second sprint within 60 days of completing a first sprint)
success_metrics.target: 45% sprint repeat rate among clients with at least one completed sprint by month 6

success_metrics.metric: Designer supply-demand ratio (active verified designers available in a given week vs. active client briefs)
success_metrics.baseline: 0 at launch; minimum 3:1 supply:demand needed to prevent brief backlog
success_metrics.target: Maintain at least 2.5:1 designer-to-brief ratio across all specialty categories by month 4

success_metrics.metric: Gross marketplace volume (total sprint fees transacted through the platform per month)

risks_open_questions: Designer supply bootstrapping is the critical constraint: clients won't convert without robust supply, but designers won't apply without visible client demand — need at least 40 vetted designers before opening client signups
Trial task quality is subjective: without standardized evaluation rubrics per design specialty, trial results may still require significant client judgment and not reduce vetting friction as intended

Off-platform relationship risk: after one completed sprint, clients and designers may transact directly to avoid the 12% fee; need to assess whether a post-first-sprint fee reduction reduces off-platform leakage
IP ownership of trial task deliverables: clients need work product rights for paid trials; designers may submit generic work to avoid IP transfer — policy and legal review required before launch
Pricing sensitivity: weekly rate transparency may expose that designer effective hourly rates exceed early-stage budget expectations; may need tiered pricing or an emerging-market designer pool
How do we handle disputes about deliverable quality at the end of a sprint week? Need a defined escalation and mediation process before launch
Geographic concentration risk: if most vetted designers and clients are US-based, international expansion requires re-running the vetting pipeline in each market
out_of_scope: Full-time or part-time salaried designer placement; DesignBid is sprint-only, not a recruiting firm
Design agency or studio accounts; only individual freelance designers in v1
Integrated design tool access (Figma, Sketch) or asset handoff infrastructure
Automated design quality scoring using AI at launch
Non-product design specialties (graphic design, illustration, brand identity) in v1
Client team accounts with multi-seat billing and role management
Built-in video conferencing; clients and designers use their preferred tools for calls
